summary: Baileys fork pulls libsignal from a mutable personal GitHub repo without pin or integrity check
details: package.json declares the `libsignal` dependency as `github:rexxzyid/libsignal-node` — an off-registry source resolved from a personal GitHub account's default branch with no commit SHA, no version range, and no integrity hash. On every `npm install`, npm fetches whatever that repository returns at install time and runs any lifecycle scripts it contains. The resolved module is required at lib/Signal/libsignal.js via `require("libsignal")` and is used for Signal E2E encryption, so it is loaded by any consumer that imports this package. The GitHub owner (rexxzyid) is unrelated to the publishing npm scope (@ubedsockets) and to the upstream Baileys project, so whoever controls that external repo controls code that executes on every installer at install and import time. There is no restriction via commit SHA or tag to prevent silent code substitution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
